rows.title: Ottawa plots ambitious plan to reshape struggling forest industry
rows.summary: The federal government released Canada's first national strategy for the forest sector on Nov. 27, backed by $6.5 billion in proposed funding over six years that was set aside in the budget. Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson called it the largest federal investment in the industry's history. The plan, which runs to 2050, aims to move the sector beyond lumber, pulp and paper into higher-value products such as biofuels, biochemicals and advanced wood building materials, while simplifying regulation, using more Canadian wood at home and finding export markets beyond the U.S. The background is a long decline: the sector has lost about four in ten jobs since 2004, and its share of GDP has fallen from about 3% to 1%, with U.S. trade pressure adding to the strain. Ottawa argues that without action, investment could flee abroad, mills could be stranded and rural job losses could deepen.
rows.fact: Hodgson announced a national forest strategy with $6.5 billion in proposed federal funding over six years, aimed at shifting the industry toward higher-value products and more diverse markets. The plan also promises streamlined regulation and more domestic demand for Canadian wood. The government says forestry employment is roughly 40% below 2004 and its GDP share has dropped from about 3% to 1%.
rows.outlook: The government warns that without action, capital flight, collapsing regional supply chains and stranded industrial assets could further hollow out rural communities.
rows.why: 미국 관세와 산업 쇠퇴에 맞서 정부가 '산업 정책'으로 전통 산업을 고부가가치 산업으로 바꾸려는 사례로, 무역과 산업 구조 변화가 일자리와 지역 경제에 어떤 영향을 주는지 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It is a clear case of a government using industrial policy to push a declining, tariff-hit industry toward higher-value products, showing how trade and structural change affect jobs and regional economies.
rows.term_def: Goods that have been processed further so they sell for more than the raw material. Turning wood into biofuels or engineered building panels earns more than selling plain lumber.
rows.note: Today's policy item (federal announcement, Nov 27 ET = Nov 28 KST). Key figures checked against the official Natural Resources Canada release on Canada.ca: $6.5B from Budget 2026, GDP share about 3% (2004) to about 1%, employment about 41% below 2004. Funding split ($2B modernization, $4B accelerator, $500M fibre security fund) matches Vancouver Sun and Vista Radio reports. Not a repeat: a separate sector strategy, not the budget, trade talks or canned-vegetable tariffs covered earlier this week.

opinion.title: Canada Forest Sector Strategy Targets 2050 Turnaround
opinion.author: Jason Ross
opinion.summary: This timber-industry analysis sets the strategy against long-term decline, noting that softwood lumber output fell 42% and pulp output 54% from 2004 to 2024 even as world demand grew, and that Canada invests only about 10% of sector GDP compared with 17% in Finland, 23% in the U.S. and 30% in Sweden. It explains the strict conditions on the biggest funds, including a secure wood supply (10 years for existing mills, 25 for new ones), a verifiable 10-year business plan, provincial backing and good relations with affected Indigenous communities. It stresses limits: the money is still only proposed, programs launch around March, and first funding decisions are expected by the end of next year. Because provinces manage about 88% of Canada's forests, their choices will largely decide whether mills get enough wood. It also reports that the U.S. Lumber Coalition sees the funding as an attempt to offset U.S. trade enforcement and vows to counter it with duties, while unions want the money to flow quickly.
opinion.why: 정부 보조금이 무역 상대국의 보복 관세를 부를 수 있고, 정책의 성패가 예산 규모보다 집행과 자원 공급에 달려 있다는 점을 보여 줘 정책을 비판적으로 읽는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that subsidies can trigger trade retaliation and that a policy's success depends more on execution and resource supply than on the headline dollar figure, which helps students read government plans critically.

rows.title: Trump's new tariffs would put rates right back where they were before the Supreme Court stepped in
rows.original_source: Yahoo Finance (Ben Werschkul; tariff-rate estimates from Yale Budget Lab)
rows.summary: The office of the US Trade Representative has proposed new tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, following an eight-month investigation into structural excess capacity in manufacturing among US trading partners. Yale Budget Lab estimates the plan would lift the average US statutory tariff rate from 11.4% now to 13.9% early next year, almost exactly the 13.8% level of February 2026, just before the Supreme Court struck down the blanket tariffs imposed under the emergency-powers law IEEPA. China faces a 20% baseline that stacks on its existing duties and could rise to 40% if talks break down, and some EU goods would go from 10% to 15%, while Mexico has been spared for now. Semiconductors, autos, steel and aluminum (covered by a separate law) and some energy and food products are exempt, while apparel, electronics and appliances are among the most affected categories. In effect, the administration is rebuilding its tariff wall with a different legal tool, which matters for US prices and for exporters such as Korea.
rows.fact: Yale Budget Lab says the proposal rebuilds the struck-down IEEPA tariff regime in aggregate using a different legal basis. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC that for most countries the changes would add only a few percentage points. Written comments are due January 5, 2027, and public hearings begin January 25, 2027, so the tariffs are not yet in effect.
rows.outlook: Capital Economics' Stephen Brown called the move less alarming than it looks but expects the tariffs to add marginally to prices and keep core goods inflation firm into next year.
rows.why: 대법원 판결로 무너졌던 미국의 관세가 다른 법을 근거로 다시 원래 수준으로 돌아오는 과정을 보면, 무역 정책이 물가와 한국 같은 수출국 경제에 어떤 영향을 주는지 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: Watching US tariffs climb back to their pre-Supreme Court level under a different law shows how trade policy affects prices and export economies like Korea.
rows.term_def: When a country's factories can make far more than its own people buy, so the extra goods are often sold abroad at low prices, which can hurt manufacturers in other countries.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: no US government, Fed or official data action was found for Nov 26-27 ET (Thanksgiving and the Black Friday half day). USTR announced the proposal on Nov 25 ET. Rates and the Jan 5 / Jan 25, 2027 comment and hearing dates were cross-checked against a Baker McKenzie summary of the Federal Register notices and a Reuters-based Investing.com report; USTR's own fact sheet did not load. Not a repeat of the PCE, GDP, durable goods or Megaspeed items covered this week.

opinion.title: Trump's tariffs have become America's new normal
opinion.author: Maximilian Hess, Fellow, Foreign Policy Research Institute
opinion.summary: Hess argues that tariffs have become normal: markets barely moved on the Nov 25 Section 301 proposal, unlike the sharp selloff after the April 2025 'Liberation Day' tariffs. He says that is because Section 301 requires investigations, hearings and public comment, so the move was expected and is much less likely than the IEEPA tariffs to be overturned in court. The proposed tariffs cover economies that account for more than half of US goods trade, with rates largely matching earlier trade deals, such as 15% for the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland. China is the exception, with the new duty stacking on existing ones as a US-China truce nears its January 10, 2027 expiry. He adds that tariff revenue now helps pay for tax cuts, so a full rollback would be costly, and he expects only piecemeal exemptions.
opinion.why: 관세가 일시적 위협이 아니라 법적 절차를 갖춘 '새로운 표준'이 되었다는 주장을 읽으면, 정책이 시장의 기대와 정부 재정에 어떻게 자리 잡는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: The argument that tariffs are no longer a short-term threat but a 'new normal' backed by legal procedure helps students think about how a policy becomes built into market expectations and government budgets.

rows.title: Real household income falls despite chip export boom
rows.original_source: The Korea Times (data: Ministry of Data and Statistics)
rows.summary: Korea's official household survey for July-September shows average monthly household income rose only 0.8% from a year earlier to 5.48 million won, which after inflation is a 2.1% fall and the first real decline in 10 quarters. Disposable income fell 1.7% to 4.3 million won, partly because non-consumption costs such as interest, taxes and transfers jumped 11%. The gap between rich and poor widened: the bottom 20% was the only group whose income fell, down 2.7% to 1.28 million won a month, while the top 20% gained 1.4% to 11.7 million won. This happened while semiconductor exports pushed GDP growth to 3.4%, showing that the chip boom has not yet reached ordinary households. Higher interest costs after the Bank of Korea's latest rate hike could squeeze family budgets further.
rows.fact: Earned income for the bottom 20% of households fell 9.2% to 248,000 won a month, and their monthly deficit (spending beyond disposable income) widened 32.1% to about 344,000 won. The ratio of top-quintile to bottom-quintile equalized disposable income rose to 5.39 times from 5.07, the first widening in four years.
rows.outlook: Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il acknowledged the uneven recovery and warned that the chip sector's growing weight could widen gaps between industries and raise exposure to outside shocks.
rows.why: 반도체 수출 호황으로 경제 성장률은 높아졌는데도 실제 가계 소득은 줄고 빈부 격차는 벌어졌다는 이 통계는, 'GDP 성장'과 '내 삶의 형편'이 왜 다를 수 있는지 이해하게 해 줍니다.
rows.why_en: These official numbers show that strong GDP growth from a chip export boom can coexist with shrinking real incomes and a wider rich-poor gap, explaining why 'the economy' and a family's finances can move in different directions.
rows.term_def: Income adjusted for inflation, so it measures how much you can actually buy. If your pay rises 1% but prices rise 3%, your real income falls about 2%.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: no major government or BOK policy or data release was found in the last 24 hours (Saturday; a planned EV support package was postponed). The Q3 household income survey was released Nov 26. Figures cross-checked with Korea JoongAng Daily the same day (5.48m won, -2.1% real, quintile ratio 5.39x); the two outlets describe the decline as the first in 10 quarters and the steepest since Q2 2023, which are both consistent. Not a repeat of this week's sentiment surveys, BOK decision or market items.

opinion.title: [Editorial] The cost of growth
opinion.author: Korea Herald editorial board
opinion.summary: The Herald argues Korea now has a two-speed economy: AI-driven chip demand has pushed exports past $1 trillion and lifted growth forecasts, while domestic demand stays weak and household loans top 1,200 trillion won. Households face pressure on several fronts, including falling share prices, weaker consumer sentiment, real wages up only 0.3% from January to August, and average new-loan rates above 5%. It accepts that chip profits may eventually spread but warns that profits concentrated in a few firms do not guarantee a quick consumption recovery. It calls for targeted fiscal help such as refinancing and debt restructuring for distressed small businesses and vulnerable borrowers. It also urges caution on further rate hikes, arguing that higher rates alone cannot fix an economy split between booming chipmakers and indebted households.
opinion.why: 수출 대기업의 호황과 빚에 시달리는 가계가 공존하는 '두 속도 경제'를 짚어, 소득 통계 뒤에 숨은 구조적 문제와 정책 선택지를 생각해 보게 합니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains the 'two-speed economy' behind the income data, with booming chipmakers on one side and indebted households on the other, and weighs which policies could help.

rows.title: Euro zone consumers sharply increase inflation expectation, ECB survey shows
rows.summary: The European Central Bank's October Consumer Expectations Survey, released on Nov. 27, shows euro zone households now expect prices to rise 3.5% over the next 12 months, up from 3.1% a month earlier. Consumers think inflation over the past year was 4.1%, close to the 4.0% Eurostat measured and about double the ECB's 2% target. They expect their incomes to grow only 0.6%, down from 1.1%, so they expect to lose purchasing power, with the poorest households expecting the biggest squeeze. The ECB watches these expectations closely because an energy-price surge can lead to second-round effects, where households push for higher wages and inflation stays high. Such effects are not yet clearly visible, but the survey adds to the case for another rate hike in December.
rows.fact: The survey covers about 19,000 adults in 11 euro zone countries. Inflation expectations three years ahead rose to 3.0% from 2.9%, while five-year-ahead expectations held at 2.5%. The ECB has all but signalled another rate increase, its third this year, at its December 17 meeting.
rows.outlook: Reuters says the jump strengthens the case for a December 17 hike, as the ECB worries that higher expected inflation and weak income growth could eventually feed into wage demands.
rows.why: 사람들이 앞으로 물가가 얼마나 오를 거라고 '믿는지'가 실제 임금·물가와 중앙은행 금리 결정을 움직인다는 점을 보여 주는 생생한 사례이기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how what people believe about future prices can shape real wages, prices and a central bank's interest-rate decision.
rows.term_def: How much people think prices will rise in the future. If everyone expects high inflation, workers ask for bigger raises and firms raise prices, which can keep inflation high, so central banks try to anchor these expectations near their target.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official ECB Consumer Expectations Survey for October 2026, released Nov 27 around 10:00 CET). Figures cross-checked against the ECB release text as republished by EIN Presswire (12-month 3.5% from 3.1%, perceived 4.1%, 3-year 3.0%, 5-year 2.5%, income growth 0.6% from 1.1%); the ECB press page itself could not be fetched. Not a repeat of this week's ECB October accounts, PMIs or French/Spanish flash inflation items.

opinion.title: THINK Ahead: The ECB's new boss has timing on his side
opinion.author: James Smith
opinion.summary: ING economist James Smith argues that the incoming ECB president, who according to ING takes over in February, arrives at a better moment than the headlines suggest. Euro zone inflation was 4% in October with core at 2.6%, a level that worries policymakers watching consumer and business expectations. Smith thinks inflation may already have peaked, citing softer November figures in France and Spain and continued oil flows from the Middle East. He finds little sign of broader knock-on effects in wage-linked prices or shipping costs and expects European gas prices to roughly halve by the second quarter. He sees a December hike as all but certain but expects no further hike in March, with headline inflation undershooting 2% in the second half of 2027.
opinion.why: 같은 '높은 물가와 금리 인상' 상황을 두고 전문가가 왜 최악은 지났다고 보는지 근거를 따라가며 경제 전망을 비판적으로 읽는 연습을 할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It lets students follow an expert's reasoning on why the worst of the same inflation-and-rate-hike story may be over, which is good practice in reading economic forecasts critically.

rows.title: China industrial profit growth hits 5-month high as recovery remains uneven
rows.summary: China's National Bureau of Statistics said profits at large industrial firms rose 20.1% year on year in October, up from 14.4% in September and the fastest pace in five months. Over January-October profits rose 16%, slightly faster than the 15.5% recorded for the first nine months. The gains are lopsided: profits at computer, telecom and electronics makers doubled on AI-related demand, while furniture makers' profits fell 52.4% as the property slump and weak household spending hit consumer-facing industries. Beijing has added liquidity and steered credit toward technology, manufacturing and infrastructure, but analysts describe the results as mixed. Strong profits may weaken the case for more monetary easing soon, while possible US and EU tariff increases and a slowdown in AI data-centre spending are risks.
rows.fact: The figures cover industrial firms with annual main-business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about $3 million). Electronics profits doubled in the first ten months, while furniture manufacturing profits fell 52.4%. October profit growth of 20.1% followed 14.4% in September.
rows.outlook: CITIC Bank International's Ding Meng said strong profit growth weakens the case for further monetary easing soon, while ING's Lynn Song called the recovery uneven and a mixed signal for the wider economy.
rows.why: AI 붐이 반도체·전자 기업의 이익은 두 배로 늘렸지만 가구 같은 소비 업종은 반 토막 난 중국 사례를 보면, 같은 경제 안에서도 산업별로 명암이 갈리는 'K자형 회복'과 이것이 한국 반도체 수출에 주는 의미를 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: China's case, where the AI boom doubled electronics makers' profits while furniture makers' profits were cut in half, shows how a 'K-shaped' recovery splits winners from losers inside one economy, and what that means for Korea's chip exports.
rows.term_def: China's official category for large industrial companies, meaning firms with yearly sales of at least 20 million yuan (about $3 million). The statistics bureau tracks their profits every month as a health check on the factory sector.
rows.note: Today's policy item (NBS official data, released Fri Nov 27). Figures (20.1%, 14.4%, Jan-Oct 16%) cross-checked against Global Times reporting of the NBS release and a Shanghai Metals Market item citing NBS (Jan-Oct total 6,737.36 billion yuan); the NBS English page was not found. India's Q2 GDP and China's November PMI are due Nov 30, so they were not yet available. Not a repeat of this week's China LPR, market-support, BOJ or Tokyo CPI items.

opinion.title: China's Physical AI Payoff: Robots, Factories and Profits (Thoughts on the Market podcast transcript)
opinion.author: Robin Xing (Chief China Economist), with Laura Wang
opinion.summary: Recorded a week before the October profit data, this expert discussion explains why AI is changing where China's factory profits come from. Xing says AI spending is concentrated in bottleneck items such as chips, chipmaking equipment and GPUs, so it is booming but still a small share of total investment. He argues this cycle could turn technology gains into real profits, because more than half of the spending upgrades existing factories rather than adding capacity, and Beijing's anti-involution campaign against price wars encourages consolidation. On that basis he sees industrial profit margins rising from about 5% to 8% over three to five years. He warns that robots do not create consumer demand by themselves, so gains reaching households depends on stable house prices and welfare reform, and he expects 2027 to stay difficult.
opinion.why: 10월 산업이익이 왜 AI 관련 업종에만 몰렸는지, 그리고 그 이익이 언제쯤 일반 가계의 소득과 소비로 이어질 수 있는지를 전문가의 시각으로 설명해 주어 뉴스 숫자 뒤의 구조를 이해하게 해 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains, from an expert's point of view, why profit gains are concentrated in AI-linked industries and when they might reach ordinary households' incomes and spending, so the structure behind the headline number makes sense.
